sa7:1.2: One time, the Buddha was staying at Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park in Jeta’s Grove of Śrāvastī.
sa7:2.1: It was then that the Bhagavān addressed the monks,
sa7:2.2: “When one delights in form, they delight in suffering.
sa7:2.3: When one delights in suffering, they can’t be liberated from suffering.
sa7:2.4: Thus, when one delights in feeling … conception … volition … awareness, they delight in suffering.
sa7:2.5: When one delights in suffering, they can’t be liberated from suffering.
sa7:3.1: “Monks, when someone doesn’t delight in form, they don’t delight in suffering.
sa7:3.2: When someone doesn’t delight in suffering, they can be liberated from suffering.
sa7:3.3: Thus, when someone doesn’t delight in feeling … conception … volition … awareness, they don’t delight in suffering.
sa7:3.4: When someone doesn’t delight in suffering, they can be liberated from suffering.”
sa7:4.1: When the monks heard what the Buddha taught, they rejoiced and approved.
